summary: What each US state bar asks of a lawyer who advertises: whether ads or solicitations must be filed or reviewed, when, the standard, late and advisory fees, the portal or method, whether an expedited review exists, and how long copies must be kept, and, where a bar states it, how many ads it reviews in a year. Every recorded field is backed by a short quote from the bar's or court's own rule or page, with the date read.

records.text: Connecticut: lawyers must file their ads with a bar or court office, by the time the ad first runs. There is no filing fee.
records.category_label: Ads must be filed with a bar or court office
records.ad_types_filed: Every advertisement to the public through any media, and written or recorded communications under Rule 7.2, plus a list of domain names used primarily to offer legal services (updated quarterly; website contents not filed). Exempt (P.B. 2-28A(b)): tombstone-only public media ads, telephone directory ads, law list entries, announcement/tombstone cards, communications sent only to existing or former clients, other attorneys/professionals, business, nonprofit or government bodies, communications requested by a prospective client, and website contents under a filed domain name.
records.solicitation_filing: Written or recorded communications (including targeted solicitations) are filed under P.B. 2-28A at or before first dissemination, with a sample envelope if mailed; no fee.
records.timing_detail: Either prior to or concurrently with first dissemination; domain name lists quarterly on the first business day of January, April, July and October.
records.advisory_detail: Optional advance advisory opinion under P.B. 2-28B, submitted not less than 30 days before first dissemination, with a fee set by the chief court administrator ($100 per the SGC FAQ); a finding of compliance binds in the attorney's favor.

records.retention: Keep a copy or recording of each communication about the lawyer's services for three years after its last dissemination, with a record of when and where it was used; electronic communications copied every three months and kept three years.

records.text: Florida: lawyers must file their ads with a bar or court office, before the ad first runs. The standard fee is $250 per ad.
records.category_label: Ads must be filed with a bar or court office
records.ad_types_filed: All advertisements unless exempt under Rule 4-7.20: TV, radio, print and internet ads (other than the lawyer's own website) must be filed unless limited to safe-harbor content in Rule 4-7.16; exemptions include websites, law lists/bar publications, communications to existing/former clients and lawyers, requested communications, announcement cards, sponsorship announcements, and legal aid organization ads.
records.solicitation_filing: Unsolicited direct mail and direct email advertisements must always be filed at least 20 days before use; the safe-harbor (tombstone) exemption does not apply to them.
records.timing_detail: At least 20 days before first dissemination; the Bar responds within 15 days of a complete filing.
records.late_fee_detail: $750 per advertisement filed less than 20 days before first use (instead of $250). A change-of-circumstances re-filing carries an additional fee not to exceed $100.
records.advisory_detail: Preliminary opinions on drafts/scripts (4-7.19(c)) and advisory opinions on exempt ads or specific website pages (4-7.19(d)) require 'the fee specified in this rule'; the Bar FAQ says the filing fee must be paid for a website-page submission.
records.portal_or_method: Online Ad Submission via the MyFloridaBar Member Portal (effective July 2026), or mail/overnight to the Ethics and Advertising Department, 651 E Jefferson St, Tallahassee, FL 32399-2300 with a check; no email filings.
records.retention: Retain a copy or recording of each advertisement for 3 years after its last dissemination, with a record of when and where it was used; for identical ads sent to 2+ prospective clients, retain one copy plus the list of names and addresses of recipients for 3 years.
records.days_detail: File at least 20 days before first use. The Bar’s own page allows a 15-day evaluation period (and 5 days for mailing) within those 20 days.

records.solicitation_filing: Solicitation communications sent by any means must be filed within 10 days after the date sent, with application and fee; for identical form letters only a representative sample of each form letter and envelope need be filed (Rule 7.04 cmt. 2).
records.timing_detail: No later than 10 days after the date of dissemination of an advertisement, or 10 days after the date a solicitation communication is sent.
records.late_fee_detail: If a non-exempt ad that was not filed comes to the State Bar's attention, it may assess a $250 fine plus the $100 review fee.
records.advisory_detail: Optional pre-approval: submit not fewer than 30 days before first dissemination the material specified in Rule 7.04(a), which includes the fee; a finding of compliance is binding in favor of the submitting lawyer. The $100 figure is the general application fee stated on the Advertising Review page; no separate pre-approval fee was found.
records.portal_or_method: Advertising Review Portal accessed through the attorney's My Bar Page (application, media upload, fee payment).
records.days_detail: File no later than 10 days after the ad is disseminated or the solicitation is sent. Optional pre-approval is requested not fewer than 30 days before first dissemination. The rule states no review period.

For mass mailings of a standard form, filing one copy of each version satisfies the rule, with recipient names/addresses kept in the lawyer's files (Wisconsin Committee Comment). Must be marked "Advertising Material".
